title: XP Can I make non pixelart assets?

posts.author: Minotercio
posts.body:
Hi! This is my first time asking something here and english is not my first language, so sorry if my explanations come out as confusing... A couple months ago i got RPG Maker XP for free and  recently i came up with an idea to make a little game. I'm an artist but i'm not used to do pixel art. I tried to import a sprite sheet of a digitaly drawn character but when i imported it, it was gigantic. Is there a way to simply make the sprite smaller? or does RPG Maker XP not allow non pixelart assets?
I'll attach a screenshot of how the sprite looks and the sprite sheet (yes, it's only the kid looking forward because it was just to see how she looked in game)

posts.author: fizzly
posts.body: Of course it allows, just shrink the image and make it smaller?

Yeah that... that makes sense. But won't the image loose quality or information? I'm gonna try it out and see how it looks, thanks for the fast reply!

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Minotercio said:
But won't the image loose quality or information?
Click to expand...
yes
but back to your original question:
all computer art consists of pixels, even 3D art has to be converted to pixels before it can be displayed on the screen, because a computer monitor can only display pixels, nothing else.
so it completely depends on what you define as pixel art, because even your original kid is art consisting of pixels.
The main limitation of XP (and VX and VXA) is the screen size, which cannot be bigger than 640x480. Currently only MV and MZ can create larger screens.
What is often called "pixel art" means an art style with few pixels and few colors. You can easily use more colors in XP, but all sprites have to fit the screen.
Usinbg 64x64 pixel instead of 32x32 is possible, or even 64x128 - but the larger you get the more of the screen is filled with the sprite, and whether you can use them depends on the style of game you want to make. In a graphic adventure like "Monkey Island" you can use larger sprite than in the default JRPGs the makers are intended for, but it also9 means you'll have to put in more work to change the engine by events and scripts.

Yes, I understand what you say. I was actually referring to pixel art as an art style, but i'm aware everything we see on screens is made of pixels. Thank you so much for your answer tho! So isn't there a way to change the resolution of an image through the script editor? I know nothing about programing but looking forward to learn. I thought there would be a way to import an image and change the resolution of it inside the program, avoiding it loosing as much quality as actually shrinking it. I'll research a little bit more about it and look if MV or MZ are better for this project and worth of buying for me. Thank you again and have a good day!

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Minotercio said:
So isn't there a way to change the resolution of an image through the script editor?
Click to expand...
no, because the pixel is the basic unit of any 2D display.
Due to historical misunderstandings, the term "Resolution" has been very abused in today's computer terminology.
A screen size is NOT a resolution, no matter what people call it.
A true resolution is basically "units per physical distance" like a printer's dpi (dots per inch).
On a display it is usually called "pixel per inch" and defined by the monitor itself - your Monito has a fixed size in inch (you don't change your monitor often, or do you?) and a fixed maximum screen size (at least in cases of TFT monitors, the older CRT monitors are probably unknown by now).
Those are physical restrictions that you cannot change, and you also cannot increase the screen size of RMXP to larger than 640x480.
Wich means more pixel create a larger sprite and you CANNOT change the resolution on your monitor hardware.
As already written above you would need RMMV or RMMZ to make your game's screen size larger, and that is the only way to increase the number of pixels displayed.
EDIT
And that only works up to the monitors maximum screen size and with some other limitations as well.
